pairs.subject: retry-backoff
pairs.evidence: crates/engine/src/retry.rs:94 with_retry_within returns success without recording the attempt count. GenOutcome has no attempts field; the only attempts field in the crate is on OverBudgetWait. So an adapter that needs three tries per call looks the same as a healthy one, and attempts-per-success cannot be measured.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine/src/retry.rs:94 Success after N attempts throws N away. Exhaustion is not recorded as its own state either: retry.rs:119 (`None => e,`) returns the last transient error, which looks the same as a first-attempt failure. Only the over-budget wait has its own terminal value.

crates/engine/src/providers.rs:136 Classification is typed and done once at the boundary, which is good (http_error/send_error are shared by the gemini, openai, openrouter, anthropic_api and http_target adapters). But the fallback branch sends any unlisted status, such as 408, to BadRequest, which is permanent and also triggers the schema-shed fallback. send_error likewise sends unclassified transport errors to the non-retryable Http variant. There is no unknown class with a small retry allowance, and unknowns are not counted.

crates/engine/src/retry.rs:132 Doubling ladder with saturating arithmetic. Each delay adds a random jitter of up to one rung (equal-jitter style, not a small ±10% wobble). MAX_TRIES and the 60 s CALL_BUDGET are separate stopping rules. A stated wait replaces the computed rung, gets up to 1 s of extra jitter, and counts against the budget. A stated wait that does not fit ends the ladder as OverBudgetWait carrying the requested seconds. The header list at providers.rs:82 is an ordered accept-list with the unit tied to each header name.

crates/engine/src/providers.rs:253 When the schema is rejected, the shed path starts a second full ladder with a fresh 60 s budget. It is not charged against the first ladder, so one intent can make up to 6 calls (generate_deterministic at line 305 does the same). There is no retry budget shared across the pool.rs parallel workers, so every worker ladders independently during a correlated outage.

crates/engine/src/retry.rs:19 Every retry is in memory and bounded to one blocking call: at most 60 s and 3 tries. No retry is scheduled to outlive the process, so a persisted retry-at schedule is not needed.

crates/engine/src/providers.rs:66 This is a client for vendor LLM APIs and operator HTTP targets, not for a replicated or leader-redirecting server with a consistency index. Side observation: the builder sets no redirect policy, so reqwest's default redirect following applies.
crates/engine/src/lib.rs:17 The only retries in this context are provider generation calls. The engine issues no credentials or leases, so there is nothing to revoke.
